                         Project Development Objectives
                         Project Development Objective (from Project Appraisal Document)

                         The project would support the government#s high level objective of sustaining growth by promoting export-diversification and an increase in value added in
                         production. Specifically, the project development objective (PDO) is to expand Argentina#s capacity to generate productive innovation in knowledge-based
                         areas by (i) facilitating the creation of new knowledge-based companies; (ii) developing specialized human capital; (iii) supporting productive research
                         innovation projects and their commercialization in three priority technology areas (biotechnology, nanotechnology, and information and telecommunications);
                         (iv) upgrading research infrastructure in the areas of science, technology and productive innovation; and (v) strengthening the policy framework governing
                         science, technology, and productive innovation.
                         Has the Project Development Objective been changed since Board Approval of the Project?

                            Yes           No

                         Implementation Status Overview
                                 A supervision of the Argentina Unleashing Innovation Project was undertaken in November 2010. The project, effective since August 2009, is being implemented by the
Public Disclosure Copy




                         Agency for Science, Technology and Innovation (ANPCyT), under the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. With the exception of component 2.2, all components are
                         under execution. US$14.4 million had been disbursed by end-October 2010, and the rate of disbursement is expected to accelerate in 2011 as the execution of subprojects gathers
                         pace.
                          Component 1.1. Six programs to provide graduate degrees on technology management started classes with 589 students in mid-2010.
                          Component 1.2. During the academic year 2009, scholarships were granted to 2178 undergraduate students of ICT programs , but a significant share of them was not renewed in
                         2010 because students joined the ICT industry or did not meet academic requirements. An action plan to address these challenges is under discussion.
                          Component 2.1 The call for proposals for "deal flow facilitators" that will support the incubation cycle of new technology enterprises concluded with the receipt of 26 proposals, 5 of
                         which were approved. The ANPCyT is currently negotiating the contracts with the winning bidders. The "deal flow facilitators will be mainly remunerated on a success basis.
                          Component 2.2. During the mission, it was agreed that the ANPCyT would conduct a competitive process to select the fund manager and the ANPCyT would present a proposal to
                         the Bank by end November.
                          Component 3. Three proposals have been approved for the biotechnology fund (in the health area), and the ANPCYT is currently signing the corresponding contracts with the
                         beneficiaries. The proposals on nanotechnology, ICT and biotechnology (linked to agriculture) are currently under review.
                          Component 4. To date, 50 projects have been approved for a value of US$24 million; 45 of these have begun execution. Disbursements are expected to pick up significantly during
                         2011.
                          Component 5. Some of the activities in the component have been revised following the appointment of a new Undersecretary of Studies at MINCyT. There are four large
                         consultancies underway.

                         Management of environmental safeguards and financial management have been rated satisfactory. Procurement has been rated moderately satisfactory.
